name: bank_import_profiles
title: Import Profiles
description: How to read one bank's export: column_map as DATA, not code. Every bank's CSV is different, so the FIRST import from a new bank is a configuration job -- paste a sample, let AI propose the mapping, confirm it, save it here. Every import after that runs the saved profile deterministically. The anti-pattern this exists to refuse: AI re-reading statements every month, which is nondeterministic and unauditable -- exactly what a fraud control must never be. AI configures; code executes.

fields.name: source_format
fields.label: Format
fields.help: v1 ships csv; ofx (FITID + balances) is the next importer. The canonical landing shape (bank_lines) is the same for all of them.

fields.name: column_map
fields.label: Column Map (JSON)
fields.help: {"date": "Posted Date", "amount": "Amount", "description": "Description", "external_id": "Transaction ID", "date_format": "%m/%d/%Y", "decimal_sep": ".", "sign": "normal"}. Use debit/credit instead of amount for two-column exports; sign=flip for banks that export withdrawals as positive.

fields.name: has_balances
fields.label: Carries Balances
fields.help: Whether this export states opening/closing balances. Without them the tie-out check cannot run and imports are honestly marked lower-assurance.

fields.name: has_external_ids
fields.label: Carries Transaction IDs
fields.help: Whether the bank gives each line a stable id (OFX FITID). Without one, dedup falls back to a content hash.

fields.name: sample
fields.label: Sample Rows
fields.help: A few real lines from this bank, kept so the mapping can be re-derived or reviewed later.
